prompt: Some young people go to college or university to have a successful career path. Others, however, chose to go straight to work to gain real-life experience after high school. Discuss both views and write your opinion.
essay:
After leaving high school, some young people decide to attend college or university because they believe academic qualifications will improve their career prospects. Others prefer to start working immediately in order to gain practical experience. Both routes can lead to success, but I believe higher education is generally more advantageous for careers that require specialised knowledge.

On the one hand, university education offers clear long-term benefits. Many respected professions, such as medicine, engineering, law, and teaching, require formal qualifications that cannot be replaced by work experience alone. Moreover, higher education develops analytical thinking, research ability, and communication skills, all of which are valuable in a competitive labour market. For example, a student studying engineering learns not only technical theory but also how to solve complex problems and work in teams. Therefore, attending university can provide a strong foundation for professional development and higher earning potential.

On the other hand, entering the workforce straight after high school can also be a sensible choice. Young people who start working early often become financially independent sooner and learn practical skills through real situations. For instance, a school leaver who joins a business may quickly develop confidence, discipline, and customer-service skills that are difficult to acquire from textbooks. In addition, early employment can help young adults discover their interests before spending time and money on a degree they may not need.

In conclusion, both university study and immediate employment have important advantages. However, in my opinion, higher education is the better path for those aiming for professional or knowledge-based careers, while direct employment suits people who prefer practical, skill-based work. Ultimately, the best decision depends on each person’s goals, talents, and financial circumstances.
